explanation: Continuous second partials require (f_x)_y=(f_y)_x. I gives -1 versus -2, so it is impossible. II gives 0 on both sides and is realized by f=(1/2)e^x(sin(x)+cos(x))+5y. III is realized by f=2y sin(xy)+xy²: differentiating yields exactly both stated first partials. Therefore II and III only are valid.
